title: Encampment response team and public space bylaw review
subtitle: Development charge deferral for a community theatre group, community safety plan adopted, and accessibility awards presented.
overview: Council approved a seven-month pilot, from August 2026 to February 2027, for a dedicated team to respond to encampments and work with community agencies. It is funded from the tax operating contingency reserve and passed {{vote:m13}}. Staff will report back before the 2027 budget on whether it should become a permanent service. Council also directed the Mayor and staff to step up advocacy with the provincial and federal governments, and asked Wellington County to discuss encampments at its social services committee.

Council directed staff to review the Public Space Bylaw and report in the second quarter of 2027, after the election. The review will consider setbacks from homes, supportive housing, playgrounds and waterways. Council moved the report from the first quarter to the second quarter. The final motion passed {{vote:m9}}. Staff expect targeted engagement, with public input through delegations once the report is published.

Council also approved a deferred development charge payment plan for a non-profit theatre group moving into a new unit. The plan runs up to 15 years with no interest. Staff will also explore relief options for non-profits in the next development charges update. The 2026-2029 Community Safety and Well-being Plan was adopted, and a closed session on a grant agreement ended with direction to staff.

decisions.detail: Staff will create a dedicated response team for August 2026 to February 2027, with a $260,000 budget from the tax operating contingency reserve. They will report back before the 2027 budget, and the Mayor and staff will increase advocacy and ask Wellington County for a social services committee discussion {{vote:m13}}.
Staff will report in Q2 2027 on revisions to the Public Space Bylaw, including setbacks from residential property lines, supportive and transitional housing, playgrounds and waterways {{vote:m9}}.
Council changed the bylaw review report date from Q1 to Q2 of 2027, which staff said gives more time after the election {{vote:m8}}.

decisions.item: Development charges deferral for theatre group
decisions.detail: Staff will offer a deferred payment agreement of up to 15 years with no interest for a non-profit theatre group's unit at 100 Crimea Street. They will also explore non-residential development charge relief for non-profits and charities {{vote:m5}}.
Council adopted the 2026-2029 Guelph Community Safety and Well-being Plan as part of the consent report.

decisions.item: Proposal to add 'structures' to pilot wording defeated
decisions.detail: An amendment to describe the pilot as covering 'structures and encampments' was defeated {{vote:m12}}.

debate: On the bylaw review, one councillor said the original proposals were too prescriptive and that a new council should handle the review. Staff said engagement would focus on community partners and advisory committees, with the public speaking through delegations. They said full public engagement was not feasible before and during the election, and that the review would displace other bylaw work.

The Mayor said residents had raised concerns about encampments next to homes, supportive housing and playgrounds, and that the current bylaw has no setback from residential property lines. Other councillors said the review should draw on more evidence and could be informed by legal developments elsewhere in the province.

One councillor asked to change the pilot wording to 'structures and encampments' because of fires and shelters built in natural areas. Staff said they understood the intent and noted that 'structures' has a specific meaning in building permits. The motion's mover said the pilot is about housing and social services, and the amendment was defeated {{vote:m12}}.

Staff said the pilot team would use existing staff at first and would combine bylaw compliance, connections to social service agencies, and cleanup of abandoned sites. A councillor stressed that the approach is not punitive. Another noted that the shortage of housing, rather than shelter beds, is the underlying problem.

On the deferred payment, the Mayor said the city cannot waive development charges outright. The theatre group's delegate said double rent and the charge of almost $30,000 created serious financial risk, and that a permit could not be issued until the charge was addressed.
